title: Animal Origin
subtitle: Some ingredients are always animal. Others never say.
description: BOTIA flags ingredients that are always animal-derived, and ingredients whose origin the label leaves undeclared.
why_body: Gelatine, carmine, shellac and beeswax are always animal-derived. But many others — emulsifiers, enzymes, glycerol, flavourings — can be animal, plant or synthetic, and the label reads exactly the same either way.
what_body: BOTIA separates two cases. Ingredients that are animal-derived by definition, and ingredients whose origin is simply not declared. The second group is not a verdict: it is the information the label did not give you.
can_1: Identify ingredients that are always animal-derived.
can_2: Flag ingredients whose origin the label leaves undeclared.
can_3: Explain why that distinction matters for the choice you are making.
cannot_1: Determine the species an ingredient came from.
cannot_2: Confirm origin when the label does not declare it.
cannot_3: Certify a product as vegetarian or vegan.
closing: Undeclared is not forbidden. It is unknown — and that is worth knowing.
